solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Academic first to smoke joint in fraternity

parts.note: a fellow is a senior member of a college

indicators.note: the first letter of the word smoke is taken, its opening one

parts.note: the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A don lights up a joint inside a student fraternity house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' looks like cannabis beside 'smoke', but it is the body's hip.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean a brotherhood or companionable association of people sharing an interest.

clue.text: Tory problem with old head of state and patron

parts.note: a Conservative is a 'Con' in British shorthand
a sum is an arithmetic problem
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician has trouble with a former monarch and a sponsor.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Latin for Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron of a shop or restaurant is a customer, someone who buys and uses its goods.

clue.text: Carriage that's departed in South East passes judge

indicators.note: the south-east pair goes past, coming after the judging word

parts.note: to hear a case is to judge it in court
SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east

explanation.surface: A coach that has left the south-east goes by a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'departed' reads as 'left', but the definition means the vehicle the dead travel in.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral vehicle carries the deceased, the departed, on their final journey.

clue.text: State burial mistakenly buries German alive initially

indicators.note: the rearranged word encloses the following letters, as earth covers a body
letters set down by mistake are in the wrong order and must be rearranged
the opening letter of the word alive is taken

explanation.surface: A state funeral goes wrong and a German is buried while still alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakenly' rearranges BURIAL into BULRIA, and 'buries' puts GA inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A country in south-east Europe, an independent nation state on the Black Sea.

clue.text: Don't scoff at all if celeb gets very obese in the end

parts.note: a celebrity is a star

indicators.note: the final letter of the word obese is taken

explanation.surface: Advice not to eat anything at all if a famous person turns very fat in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To go entirely without food is to refuse to eat, scoff being slang for eating greedily.

clue.text: Dope provided bit of optimism around North

indicators.note: the condition word and letter go round the north letter

parts.note: provided means if, a condition
N is the compass abbreviation for North

indicators.note: only the first letter of optimism, a small bit, is used

explanation.surface: A drug delivered a touch of hopefulness about the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' looks like a drug, but in slang it is inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for information or news, as in giving someone the dope on something.

clue.text: Man who leads horse away from one knight

indicators.note: the letters for one knight are taken off the drug's name

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin
the Roman numeral I is one
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A man leads a horse away from a lone knight on the battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is drug slang for heroin; chess uses N for knight because K is the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A protagonist or champion is a man who takes the lead and whom others follow.

clue.text: Ugh! Ain't sex ridiculously tiring!

indicators.note: ridiculously signals the preceding letters are put in an absurd new order

explanation.surface: Someone groans that lovemaking is absurdly wearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something that wears a person out and drains their energy.

clue.text: Pushy rector I struck with large bible

indicators.note: the letters are hit and knocked into a different arrangement

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A clergyman confesses to hitting a pushy rector with a big Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struck' rearranges PUSHY RECTOR I together with L for 'large'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible is the sacred text, the holy writings, of Christianity.

clue.text: Nobody on cocaine becomes more reserved

indicators.note: the word for nobody is placed on, following, the cocaine letter

parts.note: C is slang shorthand for cocaine
a nobody is a loser, a person of no account

explanation.surface: A nonentity taking cocaine turns more withdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone more reserved is more secretive and tight-lipped, keeping things nearer the chest.

clue.text: Adulterated drink royal knocked over by crown

indicators.note: the word is turned over, reading backwards

parts.note: regal means royal
the crown of something is its top

explanation.surface: A royal knocks over a spiked drink with his crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just joins the pieces. A lager top is a pint of beer with a splash of lemonade on top, a British pub order.
explanation.definitionFit: The beer is diluted, adulterated, with a dash of lemonade poured over it.

clue.text: Those crawling west engulfed by fumes

indicators.note: the compass letter is swallowed up inside the word for seething

parts.note: someone who fumes simmers with anger
W is the compass abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: People creeping westward are overcome by smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crawling' suggests creeping on hands and knees; here it is the front crawl stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: People doing the front crawl stroke in a pool are those in the water propelling themselves.

clue.text: Joint committee waver in the end on off-shore bank

indicators.note: the end letters are placed on, following, the bank word

parts.note: a reef is a ridge of rock or sand in the sea off the shore

indicators.note: the final letters of committee and waver are taken

explanation.surface: A joint committee wavers at last over an offshore bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like an adjective with 'committee', but alone it is a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is slang for a cannabis cigarette, also called a joint.

clue.text: Amp aperture repurposed to hold mike lead for tenor

indicators.note: repurposed means put to a new use, so the letters are rearranged into new order

parts.note: Mike is the NATO alphabet word for M

indicators.note: the leading letter of tenor is taken

explanation.surface: An amplifier opening is adapted to fit a microphone lead for a tenor singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' tells you the rearranged APERTURE takes in M and T; all ten letters are mixed together.
explanation.definitionFit: An old horn-shaped hearing aid amplifies sound for the hard of hearing, so 'amp' is a loose short form.

clue.text: One monitoring and controlling salt intake?

definitions.text: One monitoring and controlling salt intake?

parts.words: One monitoring and controlling salt intake?
parts.note: reads like a dietitian, but a salt is an old sailor, and the intake is the ships entering a port, which this official supervises

explanation.surface: A nutritionist keeps watch on how much salt a patient eats.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'salt' is a seasoned sailor, so the 'salt intake' is the shipping arriving in a port.
explanation.definitionFit: This port official regulates vessels and crews entering and leaving the haven.

clue.text: Well-trained earl will block no bidet up

indicators.note: the earl's letter sits in the jumbled letters, blocking the way through
up here means messed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An earl will stop anyone putting up a bidet in his house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is the anagram signal (messed up), making OBDIENT; 'will block' puts the earl's E inside. 'up' looks like a reversal in a down clue, but turning the letters gives nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-trained dog does what it is told, compliant and dutiful.

clue.text: Can smoke rings ultimately emit a slight aroma?

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: the curing word surrounds the final letter

parts.note: to cure fish or meat is to preserve it, for instance by smoking

indicators.note: the last letter of emit is taken

explanation.surface: A question whether smoke rings from a can finally give off a faint smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' looks like a noun after 'smoke' but is the verb of encircling.
explanation.definitionFit: A tincture can mean a slight trace or tinge, here of scent.

clue.text: Number one covered by old and glib European

indicators.note: the numeral sits inside the glib word, covered by it

parts.note: a pat answer is glib, too easily given
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The top figure is protected by a smooth-talking elderly European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' reads as a figure but means something that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A painkilling drug derived from opium dulls feeling, so it is a numbing agent.

clue.text: A contrary saying about match (not one beginning "England expects")

indicators.note: contrary means the whole assembly runs the opposite way, backwards
the saying goes round the trimmed match word

parts.note: a saw is an old saying

indicators.note: not tells us to drop a letter from the match word

parts.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie

indicators.note: the first letter of England is the one dropped

explanation.surface: A proverb about a game is contrasted with Nelson's signal 'England expects'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not one beginning England' leaves TI; 'about' gives STIAW, which 'contrary' turns round. 'England expects' is Nelson's famous signal at Trafalgar.
explanation.definitionFit: To expect something is to look out for it, to be ready for it to arrive.

clue.text: News chief must be locked in larder for nitpicking

indicators.note: the editor is shut inside the food store

parts.note: a larder is a pantry for storing food
an editor, ED, is the chief of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper boss must be shut in the larder for being fussy.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive concern with minor details and rules is fussy pettiness.

clue.text: Want heavenly body? Start to diet first of all!

indicators.note: stresses that the diet's opening letter is the one taken, and leads the answer
the opening letter of the word diet is the one taken

parts.note: the Earth is a planet, a heavenly body

explanation.surface: Wish for a perfect figure? Then begin by dieting!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' reads as desire, but here it is lack. 'first of all' just says the diet's letter goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Want in the sense of lack or scarcity, as in 'for want of food'.

clue.text: Sweet truism I concocted without trace of acidity

indicators.note: without here means outside, the jumbled letters going round the trace
concocted means cooked up, so the letters are mixed
only the first letter of acidity, a mere trace, is used

explanation.surface: A cook makes a pudding from scratch with no hint of sourness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside', its old sense: the anagram of TRUISM I goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: This coffee-flavoured Italian pudding is a dessert, which British speakers call a sweet.

clue.text: God left following confirmation in church?

indicators.note: the letter for left comes after the vow

parts.note: 'I do' is the vow confirmed by a couple at a church wedding

explanation.surface: A deity departs after a confirmation ceremony in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confirmation' suggests the sacrament, but it is the 'I do' of a wedding vow.
explanation.definitionFit: An image worshipped as a deity is a false god.

clue.text: Fall in gold corporation essentially engineers

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
corporation is an old jokey word for a pot belly, a tum

indicators.note: the central letter of engineers, its essence

explanation.surface: A slump in a gold-mining company is basically down to its engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is dated British humour for a large belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Fall is the American name for the season between summer and winter.

clue.text: Group able to restrict movement around Gulf

indicators.note: the self-controlled word goes round the gulf letter

parts.note: continent means able to control one's bowel movements and bladder
G is the map abbreviation for Gulf

explanation.surface: A band of people can stop troop movements around the Persian Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' reads as troops travelling, but it is a bowel movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A contingent is a group sent as part of a larger force or gathering.

clue.text: Grass and drugs must be hidden in case of raid

indicators.note: the drug letters are stowed inside the outer letters
the case of a word is its outside letters, R and D here

parts.note: E is ecstasy, so two of them are drugs

explanation.surface: An informer warns that narcotics must be stashed away in case the police raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' suggests an informer beside drugs and a raid, but it is the plant. 'in case of' looks like 'if', but 'case of' takes the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall water plant of marshes, a grass-like plant with hollow stems.
